S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S056.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
S056.description: Excessive anxiety and worry (expectant apprehension) occurring persistently about a number of events or activities.

subtypes.Chronic Worry: Worry occurs more days than not for at least 6 months.
subtypes.Generalized Worry: Worry is not confined to specific topics but spreads to various domains like work, school, family, and finances.
subtypes.Catastrophizing: Jumping to conclusions that minor mistakes or events will lead to irreversible disasters.
subtypes.Intolerance of Uncertainty: Unable to tolerate future uncertainty, trapped in 'what if' questions.

S057.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
S057.description: The subjective experience of finding it difficult to stop or control the worry.

subtypes.Failure to Control: Unable to regulate worry despite efforts to stop or distract oneself.
subtypes.Intrusive Worry: Worries suddenly intrude into the mind and interfere with focus while doing other tasks.
subtypes.Chaining of Worry: One worry triggers another in a chain reaction, escalating to catastrophic thoughts.

S059.name: Concentration_Difficulty
S059.description: Difficulty concentrating or mind going blank.

subtypes.Interference by Worry: Unable to focus on the task at hand because worries keep surfacing.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Attention is scattered due to anxiety, making it hard to focus on one thing for long.
subtypes.Mind Going Blank: Suddenly the mind goes empty or white, and no thoughts occur.

info.persona: Sean Windom melds a surgeon’s precision with an artist’s curiosity, channeling that blend into meticulous smile designs, vibrant watercolors, and a habit of sipping wine while obsessively arranging garden rows, even though they sometimes overbook appointments and lose track of time when painting.
info.professional_persona: Sean Windom, a seasoned dentist with four decades of clinical experience, blends a meticulous data‑driven mindset and an artistic eye, and they excel in cosmetic dentistry using digital smile design, CAD/CAM milling, and 3D printing while mentoring junior colleagues and streamlining practice operations.
info.cultural_background: Sean was raised in a small town in southern Wisconsin within a family of German‑Scandinavian descent that values hard work, modesty, and community service. His upbringing in a Lutheran‑influenced environment emphasized punctuality, self‑reliance, and a pragmatic outlook, while the region’s strong dairy‑farm heritage fostered an appreciation for nature and seasonal rhythms. Local traditions such as the county fair, fish fry gatherings, and volunteer fire‑department events shaped his sense of civic duty. This Midwestern cultural foundation blends with his personal curiosity, allowing him to balance a practical, organized professional demeanor with an open‑minded appreciation for art, new ideas, and unconventional thinking.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Sean is an avid visitor of art galleries and regional theater productions, and he paints watercolor landscapes in his home studio. He enjoys macro photography of insects and plants, woodworking projects that often produce custom dental instrument handles, and reading historical non‑fiction and scientific journals. Chess provides a competitive outlet, while hiking the local state trails and tending to his vegetable garden offer restorative alone time. He also participates in wine‑tasting clubs, volunteers at a community dental clinic, and is an active member of a local book discussion group.
info.sports_persona: Sean Windom, an avid hiker who tackles the Blue Ridge Trail each spring and a weekend cyclist on the Riverside Loop, follows the River City Sluggers minor‑league baseball team, supports the local university’s basketball program, and they keep fit through low‑impact strength training at the senior community gym.
info.arts_persona: Sean Windom, a watercolor landscape enthusiast and macro photographer, frequents the downtown Contemporary Art Museum to admire works by Monet, O'Keeffe, and local impressionists, enjoys productions by the Curtain Call Players regional theater troupe, and they capture intricate close‑ups of dragonflies and fern fronds with a 100mm macro lens.
info.travel_persona: Sean Windom, who prefers curated cultural trips, has explored the Musée du Louvre in Paris, the Uffizi Gallery in Florence, and the vineyards of Rioja, and they plan a road‑trip along the Pacific Coast Highway to visit coastal art installations and seaside vineyards.
info.culinary_persona: Sean Windom, a garden‑to‑table cook, often prepares roasted beet salad with goat cheese, walnuts, and a balsamic reduction, sears salmon with a rosemary‑lemon glaze, and they enjoy pairing each dish with a carefully selected Pinot Noir from their wine‑tasting club.

info.persona: Denise Rogers blends analytical rigor with creative curiosity, tackling spreadsheets, puzzles, and recipes with equal zeal, while their disciplined routine masks a penchant for late‑night espresso and a habit of over‑booking their calendar.
info.professional_persona: Denise Rogers is a data‑driven management analyst in Manhattan who blends rigorous financial modeling in Excel and Power BI with a curiosity for emerging tech, delivering strategic process‑optimizations while balancing meticulous organization with the flexibility to pivot under shifting project scopes, and they consistently assert their ideas in stakeholder meetings to drive measurable efficiency gains.
info.cultural_background: Denise grew up in a middle‑class Northeastern American household with Irish‑German ancestry, steeped in traditions of hard work, education, and community involvement. Living in Ridgewood, Queens, she is accustomed to the cultural diversity of the city while maintaining the modest, family‑oriented values of suburban life. She celebrates mainstream U.S. holidays and observes occasional cultural customs from her heritage, fostering an appreciation for both her roots and the multicultural environment around her.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Denise enjoys solitary and small‑group activities that satisfy her curiosity while staying grounded in practicality. She reads non‑fiction books on economics, psychology, and emerging technologies, and applies insights to her professional life. Her interests include urban photography during weekend walks, experimenting with international recipes in her kitchen, practicing yoga for mental balance, and solving puzzles such as crosswords and Sudoku. She also follows the stock market as a personal hobby and volunteers a few hours each month at a community garden, reflecting her cooperative yet self‑directed nature.
info.sports_persona: Denise Rogers enjoys a steady yoga practice complemented by weekend runs with the Queens Riverside Running Club, roots for the New York Knicks and Yankees, and they cheer on the local community garden’s informal softball team whenever time permits.
info.arts_persona: Denise Rogers captures the gritty yet vibrant streets of Queens through urban photography inspired by Henri Cartier‑Bresson, listens to folk‑rock legends like Fleet Wood Mac and contemporary indie singer Mitski while editing, and they attend off‑Broadway performances of modern playwrights such as Annie Baker.
info.travel_persona: Denise Rogers plans meticulously for overseas trips, having already explored Dublin’s historic pubs and Berlin’s tech start‑up scene on two separate business‑leisure blends, while their weekend itineraries often include spontaneous hikes in the Catskills or a ferry ride to Governors Island, and they dream of a future solo trek through the Japanese Alps.
info.culinary_persona: Denise Rogers experiments in the kitchen with dishes like spicy Korean bibimbap, classic Italian risotto, and a Sunday stew of corned beef and cabbage that nods to family traditions, favoring fresh herbs, high‑quality olive oil, and they relish the challenge of perfecting the balance of flavors.

info.persona: Gregory Jeantinor, a community‑oriented, quietly confident 35‑year‑old whose blend of practical thrift, soulful rhythm, and steadfast compassion drives both his retail ambitions and his everyday life.
info.professional_persona: Gregory Jeantinor, a seasoned front‑line retailer with razor‑sharp cash handling and POS expertise, leverages calm empathy and conflict‑resolution skills to streamline store workflow while eyeing a shift‑lead role where he can mentor teammates and infuse community‑centric service values.
info.cultural_background: Gregory’s cultural background is rooted in the African‑American community of West Tennessee. Raised in a close‑knit family where church, gospel music, and communal meals were central, he embraces Southern black hospitality and the value of mutual support. He celebrates Juneteenth, honors family histories through storytelling, and enjoys cooking soul‑food dishes passed down from his grandparents. Local Black churches and community centers in Atoka have shaped his worldview, fostering a deep sense of responsibility to uplift his neighbors and maintain harmony within his community.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In his free time, Gregory enjoys tending to a modest vegetable garden, especially growing tomatoes and herbs that he shares with neighbors. He relaxes by listening to classic soul and R&B records, finding both comfort and inspiration in the music. He frequently reads biographies of notable African‑American leaders, which satisfy his curiosity while reinforcing his practical outlook. Fishing on the Little Hatchie River offers him quiet solitude, and he volunteers at his church’s food pantry, helping to organize donations and serve meals. He also likes to work on simple woodworking projects, crafting small pieces of furniture for his home.
info.sports_persona: Gregory Jeantinor, an avid weekend fisherman who also dribbles in a modest church‑run basketball league, cheers for the Memphis Grizzlies in winter and the Tennessee Titans in fall, and prefers low‑impact workouts like gardening and light jogging over intense gym routines.
info.arts_persona: Gregory Jeantinor, a devoted listener of classic soul and R&B legends such as Marvin Gaye, Aretha Franklin, and Al Green, often hums along while tending his garden, and finds inspiration in community gospel choirs and biographical books about civil‑rights icons.
info.travel_persona: Gregory Jeantinor, a modest‑budget road‑tripper who favours scenic drives to nearby Nashville for live music, New Orleans for Creole cuisine, and the Great Smoky Mountains for quiet hikes, usually plans trips on a spreadsheet but leaves room for spontaneous detours when a friend suggests a hidden fishing spot.
info.culinary_persona: Gregory Jeantinor, a competent home cook who blends garden‑fresh tomatoes and herbs into hearty collard‑green wraps and masterfully seasons fried catfish with a secret family spice blend, delights in serving classic dishes like cornbread, sweet potato pie, and gumbo at community potlucks.
